title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident illustrates an attempt to exploit the way AI chatbots source and cite information. The operation created a fabricated institution with a large volume of synthetic reports, published rapidly, on a platform built to be indexed and cited by AI systems. The failure being demonstrated is not a model hallucinating on its own but a model being fed deliberately constructed inputs designed to look authoritative, a form of data poisoning at the retrieval stage rather than the training stage.

The point of intervention that would have caught this is content provenance verification. AI systems that surface citations without checking whether the cited organization actually exists, has a physical presence, has a publication history, or has been independently verified are vulnerable to this kind of manufactured credibility. The volume and speed of publication, 124 reports in nine days, is itself a signal that automated or near-automated content generation was used to flood the information space before any review could occur.

What is not established is whether any specific AI system actually cited the Hanover Institute in responses to users, or whether the operation measurably changed any AI output. The reporting describes intent and infrastructure, not confirmed effect on deployed models.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

Israeli-funded operatives created a fake American thinktank called the Hanover Institute to influence artificial intelligence systems toward pro-Israel messaging. The nonexistent organization published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words in nine days, designed to appear in chatbot responses when users search for information about topics like Israeli war crimes and Gaza casualties. The website was built on a platform specifically optimized to make AI systems cite its content, and it framed controversial issues in ways that consistently favored Israel's position while citing legitimate sources to appear credible.

The operation is part of a broader Israeli government campaign financed through tens of millions of dollars routed via international advertising firms, with contracts worth tens of millions awarded without competitive bidding. Israeli officials have reportedly expressed frustration that the expensive public diplomacy efforts have failed to improve Israel's standing in American public opinion, which has shifted significantly against Israel since 2022. Researchers warn that this strategy represents a new threat where foreign governments can manipulate AI training data in ways that voters cannot easily fact-check.
